newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Currency fears drain Singapore noon share activity.
newsitem.headline: Currency fears drain Singapore noon share activity.

text.p: Fears over the potential impact of weaker Asian currencies on the Singapore dollar and regional stability drained activity in the Singapore stock market on Tuesday morning, dealers said.
"Investors are reluctant to take fresh position although there are some good picks. The focus is on currency risks," a dealer with a European institution said.

Dealers said the market was nervous over the extent of the Singapore dollar's weakness against the U.S. dollar with Southeast Asian currencies still volatile after taking a battering from speculators.
The Singapore dollar has fallen to around 1.4415 to the greenback at 0430 GMT compared to around 1.4300 in early July.
"A cheaper currency might help lure funds here. But the problem is no one is prepared to move because they are afraid of how much value can be lost," another dealer said.
At 0430 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 6.34 points at 1,948.26, led by Cycle & Carriage and Fraser & Neaves.
Car company Cycle & Carriage fell 30 cents to S$13.50 while drink firm Fraser & Neaves shed 15 cents to S$9.95.
Malaysian stocks traded over the counter were particularly hit by arbitrage selling on ringgit and interest rate woes.
Dealers said news that the $6.8 billion Bakun dam project was facing a slight delay due to a disagreement between the main developer and a key contractor further dampened sentiment.
The UOB OTC index, which tracks Malaysian shares, eased 8.63 points to 1,087.48.
Malaysian KLI Holdings was active, with over three million shares. It was trading at S1.67, down five cents.
Diversified shipyard group Sembawang rose 20 cents to S$7.10 against its morning low of S$6.85 after a buy recommendation by some research houses.
Total market volume was a paltry 51.6 million shares, with 225 losers to 48 gainers.
